appraisal_events.evidence: The curé delivers an exhaustive, digressive monologue on etymology, local legend, and the church tower, oblivious to his listeners' fatigue and indignation ('sans apercevoir l'indignation que causait à ma tante'), and the passage closes: 'Le curé avait tellement fatigué ma tante qu'à peine était-il parti, elle était obligée de renvoyer Eulalie.'
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator comically diminishes the curé through his own unstoppable pedantry and social obtuseness, with the closing line confirming the effect: his talk was so tedious it exhausted his listener.

status_effects.explanation: His relentless, self-satisfied pedantry and failure to notice his listeners' discomfort undercut any authority his erudition might otherwise carry, casting him as a tiresome comic figure.
She is left worn out by the curé's interminable talk, to the point of having to send Eulalie away as soon as he leaves.
